# Incident Report — 2024-11-26 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.11.26.183** |
| MAC address | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** (from ARP) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (NBNS/mDNS), NetBIOS name **NEMOTODES**, domain **nemotoads.health** |
| Logged-in user | **oboomwald** (Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString, seen against DC 10.11.26.3) |

## Malware Family
**NetSupport RAT** (malicious repurposing of the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-access client).

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** Suricata/ET alerts fired directly on the traffic:
- `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`
- `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`
- `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin`
- `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Response`
- `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`

This is corroborated behaviorally: exported HTTP POST bodies to the C2 begin with `CMD=ENCD` / `ES=1` / `DATA=<encrypted blob>`, which is NetSupport Manager's client-server wire protocol, and the client performed a geolocation lookup at `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` (vendor's own infrastructure), consistent with NetSupport client initialization.

## Infection Chain (from DNS/TLS timeline, relative to capture start)
1. t=32.8s — DNS query for **classicgrand.com** → 213.246.109.5, immediately followed by a TLS session to that IP.
2. t=35.7s — DNS query for **modandcrackedapk.com** → 193.42.38.139 (flagged by Suricata as `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup`).
3. t=40.8s — TLS ClientHello SNI = `modandcrackedapk.com` to 193.42.38.139 (`ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in TLS SNI`), consistent with a fake-crack/mod-APK lure page.
4. t=45.4s — GET `geo.netsupportsoftware.com/location/loca.asp` — NetSupport client geolocation check-in immediately after the lure site visit.
5. t=45.7s onward — Repeated HTTP POST beacons to `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` on **TCP/443** (HTTP, not TLS, on the HTTPS port — flagged `ET POLICY HTTP traffic on port 443 (POST)` and `ET POLICY HTTP Request on Unusual Port Possibly Hostile`), continuing roughly once per minute for the remainder of the ~55-minute capture (58 POSTs observed).

This is the classic pattern for this family: a fake cracked-software/mod-APK download site delivers a NetSupport RAT installer, which then geolocates itself and beacons to its C2 over disguised HTTP on port 443.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoints (IP:port)**
- `194.180.191.64:443` — primary NetSupport RAT C2 (HTTP POST to `/fakeurl.htm`, `CMD=ENCD` protocol)

**Malicious / lure domains**
- `modandcrackedapk.com` (resolves to 193.42.38.139) — fake cracked-software/mod-APK lure, flagged by ET as a "ZPHP" domain
- `classicgrand.com` (resolves to 213.246.109.5) — visited immediately before the lure domain, part of the same redirect/delivery chain
- `confirmsubscription.com` (resolves to 52.8.34.0 / 13.56.30.207) — queried alongside the lure domain, likely part of the same ad/redirect chain (unconfirmed role)

**URLs**
- `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` — NetSupport RAT C2 check-in endpoint (58 POSTs observed)
- `https://modandcrackedapk.com/` (SNI only, TLS content not decrypted)
- `http://geo.netsupportsoftware.com/location/loca.asp` — legitimate NetSupport vendor geolocation service used by the RAT client at startup

**Files / hashes**
No malicious binary was recovered as an HTTP object in this capture — the initial payload delivery is presumed to have occurred over the TLS session to `modandcrackedapk.com` (193.42.38.139), which is encrypted and not decodable from the PCAP alone. The only exported HTTP objects are the C2 beacon bodies themselves (`fakeurl.htm`, containing `CMD=ENCD` encrypted payloads — not files, not hashed as artifacts) and benign OS/browser traffic (Windows connectivity test, Adobe update check, CRL/OCSP fetches). No dropped executable or document was observed in cleartext HTTP.

## Benign/Noise Context (not IOCs)
Standard Windows/AD/Office 365 telemetry: `*.msn.com`, `*.microsoft.com`, `windowsupdate.com`, `login.live.com`, LDAP/Kerberos/DCE-RPC to the domain controller (10.11.26.3, NEMOTODES-DC), NBNS/mDNS/LLMNR/SSDP broadcast chatter, Google/Bing/font CDN traffic, Adobe ARM update check (`acroipm2.adobe.com`), OCSP/CRL checks.
